title: The Quick Read
logline: Robin's boyfriend Kevin has one rule: he never analyzes her friends. Then Barney sprains his groin doing the splits to prove a suit is more flexible than Marshall's sweatpants, and over one long night in an emergency room, every friend sneaks Kevin into the elevator for just a quick read.
coldOpen: Kids, Aunt Robin once dated a therapist named Kevin, who swore he would never analyze her friends. He kept that promise for six months. Then your Uncle Barney did the splits.

couch.line: Not the suit, Luke. Never the suit.

guests.name: Bev
guests.role: the night-shift triage nurse, twenty-six years in, who sorts every human being she meets into colored dots and has never once been surprised

scenes.summary: Barney, who can't sit, tells Nurse Bev he was hurt saving a family from a burning yacht. Flashback: he did the splits at MacLaren's to prove a suit beats Marshall's sweatpants. Green dot. The bet is disputed, Ted the self-appointed judge plants 'and that's when I realized'. Robin brags about Kevin's rule; Kevin, the new guy, stays out of it. Lily texts him: elevator. Button: everyone leaves to stretch their legs except Barney.

beats.line: Kids, by eleven that night, we were all in an emergency room, and your Uncle Barney could not sit down.
Name and injury.
Barney Stinson. I was injured carrying a family of four out of a burning yacht.
Sweatpants are the greatest garment ever made. You can do anything in sweatpants.
A tailored suit can do anything sweatpants can do. Better. And with a pocket square.
Guys, guys. There's only one fair way to settle this. The splits.
As judge, the terms. If the suit tears, Barney wears sweatpants for a week.
And if it doesn't, I have to wear a suit. On a Saturday.
Challenge accepted.
The suit came through without a single torn stitch. Your Uncle Barney's groin was not nearly as well tailored.
So. Groin.
The suit was fine!
You're a green dot.
Green. I love green. Green is money. Green means go.
Green means you will be seen. Not tonight. But in your lifetime.
The real question is who won the bet. The suit didn't tear. Technically, that's Barney.
Ted, he's a green dot. A split isn't over until you get up from it.
The suit got up just fine. It's the guy inside the suit who's having a moment.
And that's when I realized. Nobody ever defined the word split. This is a constitutional crisis.
Kevin, you're a professional. Settle it. Which one of them is crazier?
Nope. I don't analyze friends. When I'm with you guys, I'm off the clock.
It's his rule. Six months, and he has never once analyzed any of you.
Every guy I've dated wanted to fix me. Kevin fixes people for a living, and he's never even tried.
It's the hottest thing about him. The arms are second.
To me, you're not patients. You're Robin's friends. Five completely normal people.
Kevin, I've been standing for an hour because if I sit down, my groin files a complaint.
Completely normal.
Kevin, not a read. Just a vibe. I'm the sane one, right? Blink twice.
I'm the new guy, Marshall. It's not my place.
See? He's the normal one. That's his whole thing.
Yay.
Okafor. Yellow dot. Through the doors.
Okafor? I was here first! What does he have that I don't?
A fork. In his hand.
Bev. Can I call you Bev? Is there a dot for devastatingly handsome?
Green.

messages.text: Elevator. Two minutes. Don't tell Robin.

beats.line: I'm going to go stretch my legs.
Me too. I also have legs.
Great. Everybody stretch. Rub it in. Some of us are a green dot.

scenes.summary: Kevin's office hours. Lily doesn't want a read, she needs a vault: she started the split war by lying to both sides. Ted, the self-appointed judge, gets told he narrates his life. Marshall, guilty, asks if Barney is okay inside; Kevin nearly names Lily. Barney wants a read on Bev. Button: who is Barney without the suit? Cold.

beats.line: The elevator was the only room in that hospital without a nurse in it. By midnight, it was Kevin's office.
Is this confidential? Like, legally?
Lily, I'm off the clock. I'm not giving anybody a read.
I don't want a read. I need to confess, and you're the only person I know who's not allowed to tell.
That's not exactly how—
I started the split. I told Barney that Marshall called suits straitjackets with pocket squares.
Then I told Marshall that Barney called sweatpants sleeping bags with legs.
Why?
It was a slow Tuesday.
Lily, you turned two grown men against each other over pants.
I teach kindergarten. I do that before snack time.
Okay. One observation. You didn't need a therapist. You needed a vault. You've been vibrating for three hours.
Three hours and eleven minutes. Personal best.
Thanks, Kevin. You're a great vault.
Kevin. Not a session. Just a quick read. Ballpark.
Ted. I'm off the clock.
Hypothetically. If a man is the judge of a bet and he can't rule, what does that say about him?
Who made you the judge?
I did. Somebody in this group needed gravitas.
Okay. Just one. Ted, you talk like you're narrating your life to somebody in the future.
That's absurd.
Tonight you've said, and that's when I realized, four times. Once about a vending machine.
It was a very revealing vending machine.
Also, totally unrelated. Is Robin happy?
Ted.
Withdrawn.
Kevin, I know you're off the clock, so I'm not here for me. I'm here for Barney.
He's been standing for three hours and hasn't complained once. Is he okay? Like, in his heart?
Marshall, he's standing because his groin won't let him sit.
Or. Because he's brave.
You want my read? You won, you feel guilty, and you've bought him four granola bars.
Five. I ate one. Out of grief.
Marshall, this isn't your fault. It's Lil. It's life. It's life's fault.
Life's fault. Wow. You're good, Kevin. You're one of us now.
By two a.m., there was a line. Your Uncle Barney walked the forty feet to the elevator in eleven minutes.
Next! Barney, come in, have a seat.
Sorry.
Kevin. Bro. Quick read. Nurse Bev. Flirting, or ranking?
Ranking.
Kevin, all flirting is ranking. Ranking is just flirting with a clipboard.
Barney, you did the splits on a bar so a suit wouldn't lose an argument.
The suit has never lost, Kevin. The suit is undefeated.
And who are you without the suit?
Cold.

scenes.summary: 4 a.m. Robin, journalist, clocks that everyone has changed. Kevin walks in and Lily blurts out that she started the split war, because Kevin said she was vibrating. Everyone confesses to the elevator. Robin is hurt. Marshall tells Barney that Kevin called him brave. Bev finally calls Barney: they have to cut the suit off. Then Bev wants a quick read too. Button: Robin orders Kevin to the elevator.

beats.line: Okay. Something's wrong with all of you.
Nothing's wrong. We're just tired. And that's when I real—
There! You stopped. Ted, you have never stopped a sentence in your life.
Lily has been humming for an hour. And Marshall gave Barney a granola bar.
Marshall doesn't share food. Marshall once bit me over a crouton.
It was a really good crouton.
Hey, guys. Anything happen?
Fine! I started it! I told each of you the other one insulted your pants!
Lilypad! You told me he called sweatpants sleeping bags with legs!
I would never insult a sleeping bag. I've closed some of my best deals in sleeping bags.
Lily, why would you even tell us that?
Because Kevin said I was vibrating!
Kevin said?
She came to me.
In fairness, I also came to Kevin.
Me too.
Robin, everybody went to Kevin. The man's a genius. He told me I'm cold.
Six months. One rule. And you broke it in an elevator.
They came one at a time, Robin! It was like being hunted by very polite wolves.
Aw. Thank you.
Wait. You asked about me? What did he say?
He said you're brave, buddy.
I did not say—
Brave. I knew it.
Stinson.
Finally! Bev, I knew you'd come around.
Doctor needs to cut the suit off.
No. Bev, that suit survived the splits. It's a war hero.
Then it'll die a hero.
Marshall. If it doesn't make it, tell the other suits it was quick.
Don't worry, buddy. I always carry a backup pair of sweatpants. Minnesota.
Doctor. Since you're doing it. Quick read. My husband says I rank people.
Do you?
He's a yellow.
Kevin. Elevator. Now.
Bev. What dot am I?
Red, baby. Go.

scenes.summary: Dawn. Robin explains why she loved the rule: if Kevin analyzes her friends, he'll figure out she picked them. Then she gives him her own quick read: he broke the rule because he wants a seat in the booth. He gives her one back. Undercut. The doors open on Barney in a suit jacket and Marshall's sweatpants. Ted rules. Barney wants a read on why the sweatpants feel so good; Kevin is off the clock. Future Ted swears he never narrates his life.

beats.line: Do you know why I loved your rule?
Because you hate being analyzed?
Because the second you analyze them, you'll remember I picked them.
And then you'll start wondering what's wrong with me.
Do you want my read on you?
No.
I'll go first. Quick read. On you.
On me?
You didn't break your rule because they asked. You broke it because they asked you. Like you were one of us.
You laugh at Barney before he finishes the joke. You don't want to be their therapist. You want a seat in the booth.
That's a really good read.
I read a teleprompter for a living. You're bigger font.
Can I give you one? Just one.
Fine. Quick.
You sat nine hours in a waiting room for a man who did the splits for a suit. You'd never leave any of them.
You're not afraid of commitment, Robin. You're just very picky about who gets it.
Tell anyone that and I will shoot you.
Confidential.
Not one word.
As judge, I've reached a ruling. The suit survived the splits. Barney wins the bet.
And yet. Sweatpants.
Kevin. Thursdays, seven p.m. Standing appointment. I'll bring the clock.
No.
Kevin. Quick read. Why are these so comfortable? Why do I have feelings in them?
Sorry, Barney. I'm off the clock.
Kids, Kevin was wrong about me, by the way. I have never once narrated my own life.
Dad. You're narrating it right now.
And that's when I realized.
